default.why: The design applies a seed once, at create, and marks it in the catalog (`#meta`'s resource record), so a joining copy takes its state from the log and never runs its own seed. No experiment modelled the create with its seed: a crash between the catalog record and the seed rows, or two servers that create at once.
default.closes: v4's revived-seed-row case as a regression test in the phase-1 sim, with a crash between create and seed and two creators at once

V4.why: Step 1: v4 collects a deleted row's tombstone within a heartbeat. Step 2: a fresh member applies every seed key its empty fold lacks ('fresh keys ride in'). Step 3: it cannot tell a deleted key from one the cluster never had, so the seed row comes back and LWW spreads it. STATUS.md: 2 runs of 2 on v4 63e0679, and every scale-out of a seeded resource hits it.

default.why: No address test ran on any row. default.closes: the address tests (IPv6 in brackets everywhere, listen apart from advertise, a changed private address) on the phase-1 build

default.why: Measured on prototypes of the same shape: E-02's pipeline commits many appends per fsync in TS, Rust and Go (about 2.8 M 100 B appends a second per process in TS, against v4's 250), and one shared journal keeps 740 to 890 fdatasyncs a second for 16 to 2,000 groups (E-12), the form E-11 runs under the Raft ports. The pin itself is written with the build.

ISR.why: A log file per group still commits each group's queue with one fdatasync: 1.39 to 2.25 M appends a second in Node at 16 to 256 groups (E-12, mode b), far over PERF-09's 50,000. Its weak point is the tail, 14 to 20 times the journal's p99 from 256 groups, which is PERF-08's, not this requirement's.

OBJ.why: In OBJ a commit is a PUT, and many writes share one PUT inside a commit window by design (E-41 assumes 10 ms). No experiment measured appends per PUT: E-28 timed single 1 KB PUTs (1.37 ms p50 on MinIO).
OBJ.closes: a pin of appends per PUT against a real object store

V4.why: Step 1: v4's shell calls one fsync per write step. Step 2: so n single-row writes need n fsyncs, and none is shared. Step 3: STATUS.md measured about 250 persisted writes a second per member, and 10,000 single-row writes not all on disk in 20 s, against PERF-09's 50,000 a second.

BUY.why: It turns on the base. On JetStream, the row's first base, `persisted` means one fsync per message whatever the batching: 3,668 msgs/s (E-09b), 93 % under PERF-09's 50,000. On Redpanda, which the row also allows, one majority fsync covers a batch: 175,420 records a second (E-09d).

The empty-copy clause sits at its bar: E-26's bare TS Raft host is already about 95 MB of RSS (95.5 to 95.9 MB with 16 awake groups) before `data`, L2 to L4 and the worker are added, against 100 MB, and the native and server rows have no whole-process figure at all.

default.why: Every copy and every relay holds its own client links and serves reads and subscriptions from what it folds. Followers and relays keep every subscribe property with A-06 (E-31, model-checked on ten bounds), and one Node server holds 10,000 idle links and 1,000 active subscribers on under a fifth of a core (E-27). So each added copy adds that room; the autoscaler sim itself was not run.

The design gives it: a group has `copies` voters out of n members, so a copy applies only the groups it holds, and the row's own way of spreading groups (slot moves, cells, lanes, splits, partitions) adds writers and row room. No autoscaler sim and no 8-copy run with partial replication exists: E-16 healed one group of three voters on four members, and E-18 balanced slots in a simulation of load, not of copies.

V4.why: v4's scoped replication (holders per partition) runs in its own sim tier at about 100 members, but J's 5-copy cap is today's unscoped cluster, STATUS.md lists open bugs on scoped clusters, and DESIGN-SCALE's later stages are not built.

default.why: The row has no log-only third voter. Two copies are two voters, so a crash of either stops writes, and F-11's third voter must be a third full copy (E-41 prices three machines). AMENDMENTS sections 3 and 4 say DEP-15 is lost for MIN's family and for COMP; v4 refuses two copies today.

ISR.why: SPACE says two copies plus the controller survive either crash, by shrinking the in-sync set. No experiment ran or modelled it, and the controller's own third voter is not the platform's log tier.

SLOG.why: Durability sits in a log tier of three, so two servers can lose either one by design. But the writer change (a seal and a metadata CAS) was never modelled in this study, and the shared tier's budget for OPS-14 (A-29) is not built.

OBJ.why: The object store holds every commit, so either copy's crash takes no vote away. But the lease takeover by CAS on the manifest was never modelled, and no crash test ran.

RLOG.why: The mechanism is model-checked: with two servers and crashes, one writer, no stale judgement, and a write can always commit while `#meta` and one server are up (E-16, 9 rules, all needed). With a tier shared between projects it is still open, because the tier's budget for OPS-14 (A-29) is not built; with a log tier per project it is met.

BUY.why: Its two app copies are clients of an outside log of three servers, so either copy's crash takes no vote away (by construction; E-44 lost none of 900 writes through a kill of the log's own leader). But a NATS cluster used as the platform's shared tier was never examined against OPS-14, and no crash test of a copy ran.

default.why: No row ran the host-loss test. Rows with three voters keep a majority, and a wiped replica never returns under its old id (A-01, A-28: model-checked on etcd's spec); rows that lean on a witness, a log tier or the object store for the free copy were never modelled there (V `+wit`, SLOG's seal, OBJ's takeover), and a shared tier's budget for OPS-14 (A-29) is not built. No row states the one-disk free copy's window, which is the upload lag to the object store (E-41 assumes a minute) or, with no store, the whole disk.
default.closes: the host-loss test on the phase-2 build, and a stated loss window for the one-disk free copy

default.why: No experiment modelled a hint: E-16 left out hints, leaves and drains for both `self` and `cent-co`, and `self+p` was never run (G-09, K-08). E-16 reasons that a hint that can change membership needs the controller's re-checks at the group's leader (the config epoch, 'gone' and 'alive' on its own links); those did make a stale command safe in its `cent-co` model. v5-spec's healing.py ran two `retire` hints on the draft's text, before A-01 and A-19.
default.closes: a model or sim with hints stale, duplicated and out of order (K-08), before phase 2
